findings.problem: After the edit the piece runs 4,027 words, above the standard's 2,000-3,500 target, and the argument now qualifies itself in nearly every paragraph. 'Why One still beats Three' carries five separate discounts (UIL 'self-report, told years later and unconfirmed here'; the pledge 'said it all while running for higher office'; 'one campaign-season interview ... does not prove one'; 'None of this is airtight'; 'The same discount applies to his side'), and the same campaign-message caveat already appears at the top ('which makes his self-descriptions weaker evidence than usual'). They blunt the verdict and hold down the Writing and Enneagram scores, which leaves the overall just under the release floor. This is a writing problem, not a factual one.
findings.acceptance_test: Body is at or under about 3,600 words.
